justice: The complete absence of tactile paving along the road edges severely reduces fairness for visually impaired users.
A lack of distinct, accessible curb ramps connecting the main asphalt road to the side pathways restricts mobility for wheelchair users and the elderly.
The wide asphalt roadway prioritizes motor vehicles and informal parking, indicating inequitable spatial distribution for active transport users like pedestrians and cyclists.
safety: The lack of separated sidewalks and bike lanes on the main roadway forces mixed traffic, posing significant collision risks for vulnerable groups such as adolescents and older adults.
Informal roadside parking (white cars) narrows the navigable road space and creates visual blind spots for pedestrians attempting to cross.
The installation of sturdy metal railings along the waterfront boardwalk effectively prevents accidental falls, enhancing safety for children and visually impaired individuals.
livability: The presence of the water body, wooden boardwalk, and open lawns provides high-quality outdoor recreational space that supports active aging and leisure for all social groups.
The lack of visible active street frontages, retail, or convenience amenities limits the area's ability to support daily essential needs.
The distant pavilion and scenic pathways encourage outdoor social activities and interactions, enhancing community vitality.
sustainability: The extensive presence of unpaved lawns and natural soil alongside the road provides excellent permeable surfaces for natural rainwater infiltration.
The continuous line of mature street trees and adjacent park vegetation actively supports urban biodiversity and carbon sequestration.
The absence of public transit infrastructure (e.g., bus stops) and dedicated cycling lanes fails to adequately encourage low-carbon, sustainable commuting options.
aesthetics: The orderly alignment of evenly spaced street trees with uniformly white-painted trunks creates a neat and visually cohesive streetscape.
The integration of the calm water body, wooden boardwalks, and green spaces delivers a highly scenic and visually pleasing environment.
The roadway and adjacent landscaped areas are clean and free of visible litter, indicating good maintenance and enhancing overall visual appeal.
comfort: The absence of visible benches or resting facilities along the immediate roadside significantly reduces physical comfort for elderly pedestrians prone to fatigue.
The street trees provide a moderate canopy cover, offering essential shade and thermal comfort for pedestrians during warmer months.
The open, park-like setting situated away from dense urban commercial activity provides a quiet environment, ensuring high psychological and acoustic comfort.
walkability: The lack of a designated, raised sidewalk directly adjacent to the roadway forces pedestrians to share the asphalt with vehicles, significantly reducing walkability and safety.
The separated paved pathways in the park area offer flat, well-maintained surfaces that are comfortable for leisurely walking away from traffic.
The absence of marked pedestrian crosswalks (zebra crossings) makes road crossing ambiguous and potentially hazardous for older adults with slower mobility.
bikeability: The total lack of dedicated or protected bike lanes forces cyclists to share the lane with motor vehicles, diminishing perceived and actual safety for adolescent and elderly cyclists.
The smooth, continuous asphalt surface provides a physically comfortable riding terrain without significant bumps or potholes.
Vehicles parked irregularly along the road edge introduce dooring hazards and pinch points, negatively impacting cycling continuity and safety.
